lines: a7UTILS, three hand tools built twice over: a button giving a gate and a trigger, a knob giving a constant voltage, and a detector for the edges of a clock
Raises the GATE output and fires a 1ms pulse at the TRIG output; with the mode switch at TOG one press raises the gate and the next drops it
MOM keeps the gate high only while the button is held; TOG flips the gate on one press and off the next
Sets the constant voltage, over 0-10V or 0-1V according to the range switch
Sets the range of the constant: 10 for 0-10V, 1 for 0-1V
ON passes the constant continuously; EXT passes it only while the control input is above 0V, and passes it continuously when nothing is patched to that input
Carries 10V while the button holds the gate high, and 0V otherwise
A 1ms pulse at 10V on every press of the button, whatever the mode switch is set to
The constant voltage, the knob setting multiplied by the range
With the switch at EXT, a voltage above 0V here passes the constant and 0V or less mutes it to 0V
The clock whose edges are detected; it reads high above 0.7V and low below 0.3V
A 1ms pulse at 10V each time the clock input rises past 0.7V
A 1ms pulse at 10V each time the clock input falls below 0.3V
Carries 10V while the clock input is low and 0V while it is high, an inversion of the clock
a7Utility.notes: Params 10 and 11 (WIDTH) are configured but no widget is created for them, and the code that would have read them is commented out, so they cannot be clicked and get no line. The maker's custom switch art is the reverse of Rack's stock CKSS: frame 0 draws the lever up, so value 0 is the upper or left label (MOM, 10, ON).

lines: An emulation of the Triadex MUSE: four INTERVAL sliders pick a note out of a counter and a 31-bit shift register, and four THEME sliders set what the register shifts in
Sets the internal clock from 0.25Hz to 8Hz; the machine takes a half step on each edge of that clock, so one clock cycle is two steps
Picks the bit this slider adds to the note number: OFF, ON, a counter bit C 1/2 to C6, or a register bit B1 to B31; the four INTERVAL sliders make a four-bit degree of the major scale
Picks the bit this slider feeds back: OFF, ON, a counter bit C 1/2 to C6, or a register bit B1 to B31; the four THEME sliders are combined into the bit shifted into the register at each step
Starts and stops the clock, and the lamp is lit while the machine runs
With the machine stopped, pressing this drives the clock high and releasing it drives the clock low, which is one half step of the machine each way
Clears the counters and the shift register, so a new slider setting is heard from the beginning of its sequence
ALL puts a trigger out on every step; DELTA puts one out only on the steps where the note changes
Puts the trigger on the clock's rising edge at RISE, on its falling edge at FALL, or on both edges in the middle position
REST turns the lowest note of the scale into a silence, holding the note output at its last value and issuing no trigger; NORM plays that note like any other
Every volt here doubles the rate of the internal clock
A clock patched here replaces the internal clock, and the machine takes a half step on each of its edges
A voltage above 0V here stops the machine and 0V or less runs it, overriding the RUN button for as long as a cable is patched
A rising edge clears the counters and the shift register
The note as a volt per octave pitch, a degree of the major scale over two octaves, from 0V to 1.917V
A 1ms pulse at 10V on each step that the trigger switches allow
The clock the machine is running on, 10V high, whether that is the internal clock or the one patched to EXT CLOCK
Amuse.notes: The four INTERVAL sliders are params 7, 6, 5 and 4 from left to right, the four THEME sliders params 3, 2, 1 and 0; both groups are numbered right to left. The leftmost INTERVAL slider is the note's least significant bit. The panel's slider scale is OFF, ON, C 1/2, C1, C2, C4, C8, C3, C6 and then B1 to B31, which is slider value 39 down to 0. The lamp beside the OFF position is never lit: the light loop stops at 39 of the 40 lamps.

lines: CHEAPFX, two low frequency generators for switching between two tones, each with a triangle output, a rectangle output and a gate that fades in and out
Sets the rate of that generator, 0.26Hz fully anticlockwise to 16Hz fully clockwise
Sets the shape of that generator: a falling sawtooth fully anticlockwise, a triangle at the centre and a rising sawtooth fully clockwise, and the same setting is the duty cycle of the rectangle
Every volt here doubles the rate of that generator, added to the FREQUENCY knob and clamped at four volts either side of zero
Every 10V here moves the shape across its whole travel, added to the SHAPE knob
A rising edge starts one cycle and fades the gate up; another trigger before the cycle ends buys a further cycle
A 0-10V ramp, falling, rising or peaking at the middle according to SHAPE
A 0-10V square wave whose duty cycle is set by SHAPE
Carries 0-10V while a triggered cycle runs, ramped up and down over 2000 samples so that a switch driven from it does not click
Note — the TRIANGLE and RECTANGLE outputs run whether or not a trigger has arrived; the GATE output stays at 0V until one arrives
DIVADA, five clock dividers that share nothing but a reset, with prime and power-of-two division ratios
Sets the division for that divider, snapping to 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 13, 16, 17, 19 or 23
Returns all five counters to the start of their divisions
The clock counted by that divider, which advances its count on each rising edge
A rising edge returns all five counters to the start of their divisions
Carries 10V over the first half of the division and 0V over the rest; with an odd division the low part is one count the longer
Divada.notes: Nothing is normalled between the rows, so a divider with no cable in its own input never counts.

lines: FG8, an eight stage linear feedback shift register sequencer: three rows of knobs sum the stages that are high into three pitch outputs, with a gate drawn from the same stages
Sets the internal clock, 0.25Hz fully anticlockwise to 64Hz fully clockwise
Starts and stops the sequencer; while it is stopped the gate output falls to 0V and the three row outputs hold their last voltages
Restarts the clock and shifts the register one step, and does not clear the register despite the panel printing ZERO
GAL shifts the register right and applies the taps as a toggle mask whenever the bit falling off the end is 1; FIBO shifts in the parity of the tapped stages at the top end
DELTA lets the three row outputs change on every step; ALL holds them at their last voltages through any step that generates no gate
CHROMATIC reads each row sum as a count of semitones; DIATONIC reads it as a count of degrees of the major scale
Flips that stage of the shift register between 1 and 0, which is how a starting pattern is set by hand
Adds 0 to 7 to the sum sent to that row's output while its stage of the register is high, in eight snapped steps
Includes that stage in the gate, so that the gate output goes high while the stage is high and the clock is high
Makes that stage a feedback tap; which stages are tapped sets how many steps the pseudo-random sequence runs before it repeats
Every volt here doubles the rate of the internal clock
A clock patched here replaces the internal clock and shifts the register on each rising edge
A rising edge restarts the clock and shifts the register one step
Carries 10V while the clock is high and at least one stage that is high has its gate button on
The pitch from the red row of knobs, a volt per octave, summed over the stages that are high
The pitch from the green row of knobs, a volt per octave, summed over the stages that are high
The pitch from the blue row of knobs, a volt per octave, summed over the stages that are high
FG8.notes: The ZERO button and the ZERO input do not zero anything: they reset the clock phase and force one extra shift of the register. The register is cleared to a single high bit only by Rack's own Initialize. The eight buttons in each row are numbered right to left, param 6 and param 46 being the rightmost of their rows; all eight do the same thing, so the tags are unaffected.

lines: PSYCHTONE MK II, a re-creation of the note logic of Don Lancaster's 1971 Music Composer-Synthesizer: a six stage shift register whose bits are weighed into one pitch
Sets the internal clock, 0.25Hz fully anticlockwise to 64Hz fully clockwise
Starts and stops the sequence, and the lamp is lit while it runs
Advances the register one step and puts out a gate while it is held, for walking through a sequence with the module stopped
Twelve snapped positions, A to M: A to F add this knob's weight to the pitch while that stage of the register is high, G to M subtract it while that stage is low
Sets how far this knob moves the pitch when its chosen bit is active, 0 to 12 semitones
FWD takes the feedback from stages E and F of the register; REV takes it from stages A and F
UP shifts the complement of the feedback bit into the register and DOWN shifts the bit itself; each pairing with FWD or REV runs a different 63-step sequence
POS raises the gate while that stage of the register is high, NEG raises it while that stage is low, and OFF leaves the stage out of the gate altogether
Flips that stage of the register between 1 and 0, which is how a starting pattern is set by hand
Every volt here doubles the rate of the internal clock
A clock patched here replaces the internal clock and steps the register on each rising edge
A rising edge clears all six stages to 0 and restarts the clock; with DOWN selected the register stays at 0 from there until a bit is set by hand
Carries 10V while the clock is high and at least one stage of the register matches its PAUSE SELECT switch
The pitch, a volt per octave, the three weights summed over the bits they are set to
Psychtone.notes: The WEIGHT knobs are concentric with the TUNE SELECT knobs and sit at the same centres, params 6 to 8 over params 3 to 5; the outer ring of the larger knob is still clickable, so both are tagged. The six PAUSE SELECT switches and the six register buttons are numbered right to left, param 9 and param 15 being the rightmost. The panel letters pair a stage with its complement, A with G, B with H and so on to F with M. The output jack is param-free but numbered second: output 1 is the upper jack, marked OUT, and output 0 the lower, marked GATE.

lines: YET ANOTHER SEQ3, an eight step sequencer with three rows of sliders, a gate output for each step and a quantiser on each row
Sets the internal clock, 0.25Hz fully anticlockwise to 64Hz fully clockwise
Starts and stops the sequencer
Returns the sequence to its first step
Sets how many steps run before the sequence returns to the first, 1 to 8
Sets the value of that step in its row, snapping to thirteen positions whose meaning is set by the mode switch for that row
Turns that step's gate on or off, both at the gate output for that step and at the shared gate output
Sets the range of that row in INF: 10 gives 0-12V over the slider travel and 1 gives 0-1.2V. Nothing reads it in the DIAT and CHRO modes
INF sends the raw slider value scaled by the range switch, DIAT reads the thirteen slider positions as degrees of a major scale over two octaves, CHRO reads them as semitones
Every volt here doubles the rate of the internal clock
A clock patched here replaces the internal clock and advances one step on each rising edge
A rising edge returns the sequence to its first step
Every volt here adds one step to the sequence length, added to the STEPS knob and clamped between 1 and 8
Carries 10V while the clock is high and the running step has its gate button on
The voltage from the red row, taken from the slider of the running step
The voltage from the green row, taken from the slider of the running step
The voltage from the blue row, taken from the slider of the running step
Carries 10V while that step is the running step, the clock is high and that step's gate button is on
YASeq3.notes: The row outputs carry a volt per octave pitch in the DIAT and CHRO modes and a plain 0-12V or 0-1.2V in INF, so the pitch colour describes two of the three modes. The code's comments on the three mode branches name them the other way round: the branch commented diatonic reads the chromatic table and the one commented chromatic reads the diatonic table. The panel labels match what the code does.
